name: Slant 6
label: Dischord
lede: Named for a Chrysler engine, powered by a 1963 Silvertone and a drummer who learned to play just to join: three years, two albums, and a record the New York Times would call arguably the best of the riot grrrl era.

eras.title: A slant six and a Silvertone
eras.text: After Autoclave, Christina Billotte wanted something simpler and faster. She found it in a trio with bassist Myra Power and Marge Marshall, an English trumpet player who agreed to learn the drums, and in a scene of house parties and fashion shows run with Nation of Ulysses.

q: Something more straightforward than Autoclave, more danceable.
years.h: Slant 6 starts, with a drummer learning on the job
years.p: [[Christina Billotte|62325e5d-014f-42a1-90d5-fa12e17aa214]] of [[Autoclave|1f5b789d-afaf-45ca-a0d6-87502dcef08f]] plays guitar and sings, [[Myra Power|90cf6dcb-e8f5-4b69-be33-3e365b6be4ae]] plays bass. Marge Marshall, an English trumpet and piano player, learns the drums after the band talks her into it, per Bandcamp Daily.
years.xp:
The name comes from Chrysler's slant-six engine, a nod to what Bandcamp Daily called the golden age of the American auto industry. Billotte played a 1963 Silvertone through the band's whole run, and the sound landed somewhere between post-punk austerity, surf twang and Link Wray rumble.

Billotte has said she wanted major-key songs and more energy this time, a deliberate turn from Autoclave's knots.

years.h: Slant 6 and Nation of Ulysses throw the Famous Monsters parties
years.p: Dischord says Slant 6 worked with members of [[Nation of Ulysses|ae888df0-2a19-4895-a654-e0093875d5b6]] on recordings, fashion shows and a run of performance house parties called Famous Monsters.

years.h: Slant 6's What Kind of Monster Are You? 7" · Dischord No. 85
years.p: Slant 6's debut single. Wikipedia dates it 1993; Bandcamp Daily says early 1994.
yt: "What Kind of Monster Are You?" live

eras.title: Soda Pop * Rip Off
eras.text: Slant 6's debut album packed thirteen songs into 34 minutes, with hooks where nobody expected them. The Chicago Reader compared the band to early Wire: no excess, say the bit and move on.

years.p: Slant 6's debut album: thirteen songs in 34 minutes, produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]. Bandcamp Daily hears the Wipers, Wire, the Gories and the Breeders in it; Rolling Stone singled out the groove of Time Expired.
Slant 6 appear in Half-Cocked, the 1994 cult indie road movie, per Wikipedia, a snapshot of the band at full speed.

eras.title: Inzombia, England, and the end
eras.text: Inzombia, Slant 6's second album, was stranger and darker. Then came the band's only trip to England, supporting Fugazi in rooms far bigger than any D.C. house party, and Slant 6 broke up before it ended.

years.p: Slant 6's second album, recorded at Inner Ear and produced by the band and Ian MacKaye. Twelve songs, from G.F.S. to the title track, with Retro Duck and Eight Swimming Pools along the way.
Slant 6 share a Time Bomb Records single with The Make-Up, Ian Svenonius and James Canty's band after Nation of Ulysses, per Wikipedia. The Famous Monsters crew on one record.

years.h: Slant 6 open for [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] in Manchester, England
years.p: The Fugazi Live Series logs Slant 6 and Fabric supporting Fugazi at the Manchester Academy, the night after Brighton, in front of 1,200 people.

years.h: Slant 6 play their last show in Leeds
years.p: Dischord says Slant 6 broke up on their 1995 English tour with Fugazi, after a final show in Leeds. Christina Billotte goes on to [[Quix*o*tic|e4ad9a5b-7358-46be-9d34-73e9b9d072ec]] and [[The Casual Dots|d74e8159-d217-4a24-8ef0-5c2aab85a308]].

eras.title: Arguably the best
eras.text: No reunion, just the records, and a slow critical climb until the big papers caught up with what DC fans had said all along.

years.p: Washington City Paper's review of the reissue says Christina Billotte was still a better singer than many of her '90s contemporaries. Mary Timony, her Autoclave bandmate, has called Slant 6 one of her all-time favourite groups.

years.big: The best album of the riot grrrl era?
q: One of my all-time favourite groups.
years.src: New York Times · Rolling Stone · Pitchfork
years.h: The New York Times on Slant 6's Soda Pop * Rip Off
years.p: The New York Times calls Slant 6's Soda Pop * Rip Off arguably the best album of the riot grrrl era.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's Rob Sheffield has called it an essential LP of the nineties, and Pitchfork an enduring model of punk rock poise.
